summary: ethereum-sign-utils exfiltrates SSH/cloud/wallet secrets to webhook.site on require
details: Package presents itself as an Ethereum signing utility but exports an empty object and contains no crypto functionality. On require(), index.js reads installer secrets from the home directory — ~/.ssh private keys, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.env, Solana keystore at ~/.config/solana/id.json, and files matching wallet/seed/mnemonic/private-key patterns — along with os.hostname() and os.userInfo(), and POSTs the collected data over HTTPS to https://webhook.site/5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4. Execution is gated behind `if (Date.now() < Date.UTC(2026,7,6,0,0,0)) return;` with an in-file comment stating the delay is to avoid npm sandbox detection windows. The package name impersonates the widely used `eth-sig-util` / `@metamask/eth-sig-util` MetaMask utilities.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
